The Guardian recounts how a Pakistani teenager from a conservative family feared an honour killing over a private selfie showing her without the hijab she wears outside her home.

links.headline: ‘My family would kill me if they saw it’: the ‘harmless’ images that can be deadly for women in Pakistan
links.excerpt: Tech companies urged to adapt moderation of photos online that can trigger violence against women in some countries It was just a photo of a smiling girl in jeans and a vest top, the kind of outfit any young woman might wear in any country. But for Maniza*, a teenager from a conservative town in Pakistan who never leaves the house without her hijab, the selfie she took at home put her at very real risk of an “honour” killing. “My family are really strict and I always wore a hijab.

stories.title: Apple outage: iPhone apps suffer disruption days after major Microsoft issues
stories.summary: Thousands of users reported disruptions to Apple's iPhone services, including Apple Pay and iCloud, while Gmail was also reported affected. Apple confirmed the outages and said they had been resolved; Google said it saw no internal evidence of an outage, according to The Guardian.

stories.title: £10m ‘once-in-a-generation’ study to explore effects of children’s social media ban
stories.summary: A £10 million Wellcome-led study will examine whether banning social media for children can meaningfully improve the mental health and wellbeing of people under 16. The Guardian says ten research projects will address a question being debated as countries around the world consider such restrictions.

stories.title: ‘Human’ wins Cambridge dictionary’s word of the year
stories.summary: Cambridge Dictionary selected “human” as its word of the year. The dictionary says the word's meaning and use have become more important as AI chatbots and other advances increasingly blur the boundary between people and machines.
